# Problem 7 · How often does each criterion pick noise as "best"? (simulation)

> (a) Bring across the walkthrough loop (response unrelated to three predictors,
> `set.seed(126)`, 500 reps) and its four proportions. (b) Add the strict rule:
> accept the AICc winner only if it beats the runner-up by more than 2 units.
> Record how often a winner is more than 2 clear, how often that winner still
> holds a noise predictor, and the overall rate. (c) Explain how the strict rule
> lowers the false-positive rate, using the median gap. (d) Repeat for BIC and
> fill in the comparison table. (e) Explain why BIC declares a clear winner more
> often, and how it can be both more trustworthy when it commits and more often
> confidently wrong overall.

**My work:**

```{r}
set.seed(126)
n <- 50; a <- 5; sdy <- 3
nummodels <- 500
pstor <- AICstor <- AICcstor <- BICstor <- rep(NA, nummodels)
noise_top <- gap <- rep(NA, nummodels)
for (i in 1:nummodels) {
  y <- rnorm(n, mean = a, sd = sdy)
  x1 <- runif(n); x2 <- runif(n); x3 <- runif(n)
  d <- data.frame(y, x1, x2, x3)
  reg <- lm(y ~ ., data = d)
  pstor[i]    <- sum(summary(reg)$coefficients[2:4, 4] < 0.05)
  AICstor[i]  <- sum(!is.na(dredge(reg, rank = "AIC")[1, 2:4]))
  dd          <- dredge(reg, rank = "AICc")
  AICcstor[i] <- sum(!is.na(dd[1, 2:4]))
  noise_top[i] <- AICcstor[i]
  gap[i]       <- dd$AICc[2] - dd$AICc[1]
  BICstor[i]  <- sum(!is.na(dredge(reg, rank = "BIC")[1, 2:4]))
}
data.frame(p = mean(pstor > 0), AIC = mean(AICstor > 0),
           AICc = mean(AICcstor > 0), BIC = mean(BICstor > 0))
# Your strict-rule summaries and the BIC comparison here
```

# Problem 8 · When BIC misses a weak-but-real effect (simulation)

> Three predictors with known effects (strong 0.8, modest −0.4, weak 0.1;
> `set.seed(11)`, n = 60). (a) Run the single simulation and report which
> predictors each criterion keeps. (b) Wrap it in a 500-rep loop and report the
> retention proportion of each predictor under AIC, AICc and BIC. (c) Say which
> criterion you would use for "is the weak predictor worth studying further?"
> and which for "does the weak signal generalize?". (d) Rerun (b) and the
> Problem 7 noise loop at n = 500, fill in the power / Type I table, and explain
> the two behaviours from the penalties 2 and ln n.

**My work:**

```{r}
set.seed(11); n <- 60
strong <- runif(n); modest <- runif(n); weak <- runif(n)
y <- 0.8*strong - 0.4*modest + 0.1*weak + rnorm(n, 0, 0.5)
d <- data.frame(y, strong, modest, weak)
m <- lm(y ~ strong + modest + weak, data = d)
dredge(m, rank = "AIC"); dredge(m, rank = "AICc"); dredge(m, rank = "BIC")
# Your 500-rep loop here
```

# Problem 9 · AIC vs LOOCV on the trophic-position data (qcbs_w6_data.csv)

> Rank the six candidate fixed-effect models by AICc and by LOOCV MSE
> (`cv.glm`). (a) Report the table; do the two criteria agree? (b) Compute
> $\Delta$AICc and Akaike weights; is there a cluster within 2 units? (c)
> Compare the best model's LOOCV MSE to `var(dat$Trophic_Pos)`. (d) Say which
> criterion you would trust for pure prediction, and one way AICc could mislead
> at this sample size.

**My work:**

```{r}
forms <- list(
  null     = Trophic_Pos ~ 1,
  length   = Trophic_Pos ~ Z_Length,
  len_sp   = Trophic_Pos ~ Z_Length + Fish_Species,
  len_lk   = Trophic_Pos ~ Z_Length + Lake,
  full     = Trophic_Pos ~ Z_Length + Fish_Species + Lake,
  interact = Trophic_Pos ~ Z_Length * Fish_Species + Lake)
cv   <- sapply(forms, function(f) cv.glm(dat, glm(f, data = dat))$delta[1])
aicc <- sapply(forms, function(f) AICc(glm(f, data = dat)))
data.frame(cv_MSE = round(cv, 4), AICc = round(aicc, 1))
# Your weights and variance comparison here
```
